ios.desc:
Corante is a news reader for people who would rather not be measured.

Follow any site that publishes a feed — newspapers, blogs, magazines, a friend's website — and read everything in one timeline, in the order you choose, without an algorithm deciding what you see.

PRIVATE BY ARCHITECTURE, NOT BY PROMISE

Corante has no server. Your subscriptions and reading history live in your own private iCloud database, which belongs to your Apple Account. The developer cannot read it, and never receives it.

Your devices fetch feeds directly from the publishers, the same way a browser would. Nothing is relayed through anyone in between, because there is no in between.

There is no account to create, no email address to hand over, and no password to forget. Install it and start reading.

SYNCS EVERYWHERE, SILENTLY

Add a feed on your Mac and it is on your iPhone before you pick it up. Read an article on the train and it is marked read on your iPad at home. Star something on your Apple Watch and it is waiting for you later.

CLEAN READING

Most feeds give you two lines and a link. Corante fetches the article and extracts the text, so you read the piece rather than the page it was buried in. Articles render with JavaScript switched off, which removes every analytics beacon, tracking pixel and consent wall in one step.

SEARCH EVERYTHING YOU HAVE READ

Corante indexes the full text of every article on your device as it arrives.
Search finds words from the middle of a piece, not just its headline, and it
works with no network connection — the index is yours, on your device.

BUILT FOR MORE THAN ENGLISH

Text direction is resolved per article rather than per app, so a right-to-left headline and a left-to-right one sit correctly in the same list. The article decides, not your device.

THREE WAYS TO READ

Compact for scanning a lot quickly. Cards for a balance of headline and image. Mosaic for a magazine feel, with headlines set over the artwork.

Two looks, each with its own light and dark: Modern, or Newsprint — warm paper, sepia ink and serif type throughout.

BRING YOUR SUBSCRIPTIONS

Import an OPML file from any other reader and pick up where you left off. Export it whenever you like. Your list is yours to take elsewhere.

FINDING THINGS TO READ

You do not need to hunt for a feed address. Type a publication's name and Corante checks its own built-in list of well-known sources, then tries the website itself — both without asking anyone else. An optional online lookup
